answer: Each identity must tie its claim with a velvet cord: part the velvet and every fiber is one of its own verified jobs — a single borrowed fiber frays under challenge and drops the claim. The claim stands one full epoch on a ridge, a high line visible to all. During that epoch a gale blows: any peer may throw challenges at the claim, and the gale squares with every voice — one voice faces one challenge, two face four, three face nine. Ten voices need ten cords and a hundredfold gale, so no cord can be lent to a clone.
